video.title: The Most Useful AI Tool You’ve Never Heard Of

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Jay, founder of Violoop, a $399 (Kickstarter) on-device AI agent box that watches your screen via USB-C, builds a private memory graph, drafts replies and documents, and runs tasks while you're away. Jay demos invoice logging, an email-to-QuickBooks quotation workflow and ad performance tracking, claiming users save about two hours a day. They discuss using AI context to find a business, Marketplace arbitrage, cheap storefront tests and localising open-source AI tools for Asian markets. The episode is largely a product promotion.

tactics.name: Automate invoice capture
steps: Connect Gmail to the agent
When an invoice email arrives, scan it
Log date, amount and attachment in a Google Sheet
Send sheet to accountant at tax time

tactics.name: Email-to-quotation workflow
steps: Agent detects quote request email
Asks permission
Pulls latest prices and reseller discount from Google Sheet
Builds PDF quote in QuickBooks
Drafts reply with PDF for human to send

tactics.name: Ad performance dashboard and creative refresh
steps: Pull data from Meta, Google, X
Track views, CPA, CTR per ad
Cut underperformers
Generate new images/videos to test

tactics.name: Find a business from your own behaviour
steps: Let an AI observe what you consume
Ask it what you spend time on
Mine comments on niche videos for pain points

tactics.name: Triage DMs with an agent
steps: Monitor DMs and log to a Google Sheet
Search for high-value ones (podcast invites, success stories)

tactics.name: Run many cheap tests
steps: Build multiple simple storefronts
Share with friends and groups
Keep the one that gets positive feedback

warnings.warning: Small on-device models are still far less capable than frontier models (GPT-3.5/4 level).

quote.text: they're still not as capable as the frontier the open AI the anthropic models
quote.speaker: Jay

warnings.warning: Irreversible agent actions (deleting files, sending messages) should require user permission.
Kickstarter price will rise; early-bird urgency is promotional.

lessons.lesson: AI agents mostly let you do more work, not less: an 8-hour day yields 16-30 hours of output.

quote.text: my eight hour workday still looks like an eight hour [music] workday
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: 'What business should I start' requires deep personal context; your consumption habits reveal niches.
Pain points for a niche are often already in comments on niche videos.

quote.text: the answer is probably already in the comments
quote.speaker: Jay

lessons.lesson: The cost of building a storefront is near zero; run many trials until one clicks.
Technology is unevenly distributed: localise existing tools for markets not yet exposed.
Subscription fatigue is real; users dislike many $20 monthly bills.
Agents should ask permission before irreversible actions.

evidence_quality.rationale: Founder promoting his own pre-launch product; claims (2 hours/day) are self-reported survey figures.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Guest is the founder selling Violoop on Kickstarter.
